message.reasoning:
The user wants me to compare two photos of a turkey in a roasting pan and determine what changed.

Let me look carefully at both images.

Image 1: Turkey inside the oven. I see the roasting pan on the rack. The turkey has a temperature probe inserted. Let me look at the probe. In image 1, the probe (the metal wire/stick) appears to be inserted into the left side of the turkey (from viewer's perspective), with the wire looping up to the left. Actually, let me look. There's a thin wire coming from the left side, looping up, and a metal probe sticking into the turkey near the center-left.

Image 2: Turkey on the stovetop (removed from oven). The probe is now on the left side of the turkey (viewer's left), with the wire going off to the left/bottom.

Let me look at the orientation of the turkey. In image 1, the turkey's breast is facing the viewer, and the legs are on the right side? Let's look. In image 1, I see the rounded breast at top, and on the right there's a leg/drumstick pointing right. On the left there's some meat too.

In image 2, the breast is on the left, and the leg/drumstick is on the right pointing up-right. Hmm.

Let me look more carefully at distinguishing features.

In image 1: The breast (big rounded part) is at the top center. There's a drumstick/leg on the right side (the long bone pointing right). On the left side there's a flap of meat (wing?). The probe is inserted in the middle-left area.

In image 2: The big rounded breast is on the left. The drumstick/leg is on the right pointing up. The wing/flap is on the bottom left. The probe is inserted in the center with wire going left.

Hmm, this is tricky. Let me think about rotation. If the turkey was rotated 180 degrees, the breast that was facing forward would now face backward, so we'd see the back side. But in image 2 we still see a big rounded breast-looking side. Actually when you rotate a turkey 180 degrees in a pan, the side that was facing you now faces away, and you see the opposite side.

Let me look at the legs. In a typical trussed turkey, the legs point toward the viewer (front) or to the sides. Hmm.

Let me look at the position of the probe relative to the turkey's anatomy, not the viewer.

In image 1, the probe is inserted into the leg/thigh on the viewer's left? Or into the breast? It looks like it's stuck into the meat on the left-center.

In image 2, the probe is inserted into the leg/thigh on the viewer's right-center? The probe tip is in the middle, with the wire coming from the left.

Let me look at the wire path. In image 1, the wire comes from the left edge, loops up high, and the probe goes down into the turkey. So the probe is on the left side.

In image 2, the wire comes from the probe and goes down-left off the pan. The probe is inserted in the middle.

Hmm, I need to look at the legs more carefully.

Let's define the turkey's body. A turkey has two legs (drumsticks) and two wings. In image 1, I see one drumstick clearly on the right (the long pinkish bone with skin). On the left I see what might be the other leg or a wing tip.

In image 2, I see a drumstick on the right (long, pointing up-right) and a wing tip on the bottom left (the little flap). The big round breast is on the left.

So in image 1, the breast is at top, drumstick on right. In image 2, breast on left, drumstick on right. That doesn't look like a 180 rotation.

Wait, maybe I'm misreading image 1. Let me look again. In image 1, the rounded breast is at the top. The right side shows a drumstick (long bone). The left side shows... a darker piece of meat, maybe a wing or the other leg folded.

In image 2, the rounded breast is on the left (big shiny dome). The right side shows a drumstick. The bottom left shows a wing tip.

Hmm if in image 1 breast is top and in image 2 breast is left, that's a 90 degree rotation, not 180.

But the choices only offer "rotated 180" or "not rotated". So I need to decide between those.

Let me look at the probe position relative to anatomy. The key in the choices is whether the probe moved from one leg to the other, and whether the turkey rotated.

Let me look at the probe in image 1: it's inserted into the leg on the viewer's left (the meaty part on left). In image 2: the probe is inserted into the leg on the viewer's right? Actually in image 2 the probe tip seems to be in the center of the breast/leg boundary.

This is too detailed. Let me think about typical answer. The probe wire in image 1 loops on the left. In image 2 the wire goes to the left as well. If the turkey were rotated 180, and the probe stayed in the same physical leg, then the probe would appear on the opposite side from the viewer.

Let's think: In image 1, probe on viewer-left. If turkey rotates 180 (around vertical axis), then the physical part that was on viewer-left now is on viewer-right. So if probe stayed in same physical leg, it would now appear on viewer-right. In image 2, the probe appears... center-left? The wire goes left. Hmm.

Alternatively if probe moved to other leg and turkey rotated 180, the probe would appear on viewer-left again.

Let me look at the legs in each image to identify which physical leg.

I'll look at the drumstick shape. In image 1, the visible long drumstick is on the right. In image 2, the visible long drumstick is on the right. If the turkey did NOT rotate, then the same drumstick is on the right in both. In image 1 the probe is on the left (the other leg). In image 2 the probe is on the... the probe tip is in the middle, near the left drumstick area? The wire comes from left.

Ugh, I'm spending too much time. Let me look at the overall orientation of the breast. The breast is the big smooth dome. In image 1, the dome's orientation: the rounded part faces up and slightly toward viewer. In image 2, the dome is on the left facing left-ish.

Actually, you know, maybe in image 1 the turkey is positioned with breast toward viewer, legs toward the back/sides. When you take it out and rotate 180, the breast faces away and you see the back (the cavity side). But image 2 shows a smooth dome which looks like breast, not the bony back.

Hmm wait, in image 2 the big dome on the left could be the breast seen from a side angle. If rotated 180, the breast would be on the far side, and we'd see the back on the near side. The back of a turkey (cavity) is flatter and bony, not a smooth dome. The smooth dome in image 2 suggests breast is on the near side, so NOT rotated 180.

But then the orientation differs (top vs left), which would be a 90 rotation, not in options. So maybe "not rotated" is the intended because the breast is still facing the viewer generally.

Let's look at the legs again. In image 1, the legs (drumsticks) appear to be pointing toward the viewer and to the right? The right drumstick points right. In image 2, the right drumstick points up-right. The left side in image 2 has a wing tip (the small flap with the pointed end). In image 1, the left side has a darker flap which could be the same wing tip.

So if the wing tip is on the left in both, the turkey is NOT rotated. Good. That matches "not rotated".

Now the probe: In image 1, the probe is inserted into the left side (the leg/wing area on left). In image 2, the probe is inserted into the right side? Let's look. In image 2, the probe (the metal rod) goes from center to the right-ish, into the meat on the right-center (the leg that's pointing toward viewer at bottom). The wire loops from the probe's tail to the left.

Hmm in image 1, the probe rod goes from top-left (wire) down into the turkey at center-left. So probe tip at center-left.

In image 2, the probe rod goes from left (wire tail at center-left) into the turkey at center-right. So probe tip at center-right.

So if turkey not rotated, probe tip moved from left to right = moved from one leg to the other. That matches option C: "not rotated. The temperature probe was moved from one leg to the other."

Let me double check by examining the probe in image 1: I see a thin wire coming from upper-left, curving, and a straight metal probe (the temperature probe stem) going down into the turkey at the center-left, into the meaty leg. Yes.

In image 2: I see a thin wire (the cable) coming from the probe and going off to bottom-left. The probe stem goes from center-left to center-right into the turkey, into the leg that's in the front (the drumstick pointing at viewer). So the probe is now in the front/right leg.

In image 1, the front/right leg (the long drumstick on right) did NOT have the probe; the probe was in the left leg. So yes, probe moved from one leg to the other.

Thus option C.

Let me sanity check option A: probe not moved. If probe not moved and turkey not rotated, then probe should be in same visual position (left leg). But in image 2 probe is in the front/right leg. So moved. So A wrong.

Option C fits.

Thus answer C.

I'm fairly confident: turkey not rotated (wing tip and breast orientation consistent enough), probe moved.

Let me double check the "not rotated" by comparing the position of the big breast dome relative to the pan. In image 1, the breast dome is at the far side of the pan (top), with legs toward the near side? Hmm the drumstick on right is at the near-right. In image 2, the breast dome is at left, drumstick at right. If not rotated, the breast should be at same side of pan. In image 1 breast at top (far), in image 2 breast at left. That's a 90-degree difference in pan orientation? But the pan itself is round, so we can't tell rotation of pan. The turkey's orientation relative to viewer: in image 1 we look at the turkey from the front of the oven (front of turkey toward viewer). In image 2 the turkey is on the stove, also viewed from front. If not rotated when removed, the front of turkey should still face the viewer (the same direction it faced in oven, assuming it was taken out and set down without turning). In the oven, the front of turkey (breast) faced the viewer. When removed and placed on stove, if not rotated, the breast should still face the viewer. In image 2, the breast dome is on the left, meaning we're seeing the turkey from its side? That suggests a 90-degree turn, not 180.

Hmm but the options only give 180 or not. The "not rotated" might be loosely meaning not turned around 180. The visual difference in angle might just be camera angle difference (the second photo taken from a different position, e.g., from the side). The second photo looks like it's taken from a higher, more side-on angle. The breast dome appearing on left could be due to camera being to the right of the turkey.

Given the camera in image 2 is positioned to the right (we see the stovetop on left, oven on right; the pan is on the front burner; the camera looks from front-left? hard to say). The perspective is different.

The most salient change that the question wants us to detect is the probe moving from one leg to the other. Because in image 1 the probe is clearly in one leg (left), in image 2 clearly in the other leg (the front drumstick). And the turkey's general orientation (breast toward viewer) is roughly the same, not flipped 180 (if flipped 180 we'd see the back/cavity).

Thus C.

I'll commit to C.
